subject: POC readiness & quick-close checklist: org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Tan <claire.tan@orbhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC readiness & quick-close checklist: org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short, actionable checklist so we can keep the POC on a two-week runway and avoid back-and-forth. If you can confirm the items below and loop in procurement/security as needed we can lock dates for the presales session and start provisioning.

POC quick-close checklist (high level):
- Org invite: add a service account admin in your org (recommended: svc-redwood-poc@orbhealth.com) so we can bind roles and create mapping for observability.
- API keys: we provide API key creation steps; you can either create short-lived keys or request a scoped key. We need at least one key for the evaluation (read-write generation + limited quota).
- IP allowlist: please confirm one or two CIDR ranges to whitelist. Sample CIDRs attached as a reference.
- VPC peering: if you want private peering, share your VPC ID, region, and preferred maintenance window. We can initiate peering and provide the peering acceptance template.
- Procurement: estimated MRR/credit terms are in the attached MAP doc for sign-off.

Attachments: MAP-ORBHealth-v1.0.pdf (mutual action plan + dates), redwood-network-sample-cidrs.txt (example allowlist ranges)

Next steps: can you confirm the contact for procurement and security today? If we get that, Marissa will schedule a short runbook call with your infra team and we’ll aim to kick provisioning on Mon, Mar 15.

Thanks — I’ll keep this lightweight.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0162

From: Claire Tan <claire.tan@orbhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orbhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC readiness & quick-close checklist: org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Ben —

Appreciate the concise checklist. I confirmed internally and here's the status:
- Org invite: will do today. I’ll add the suggested service account (svc-redwood-poc@orbhealth.com) and cc: security@orbhealth.com.
- API keys: procurement prefers scoped keys with 30-day TTL; we’ll create one and share the key through our secret-sharing pipeline (I’ll send the location once created).
- IP allowlist: we can start with 34.82.0.0/16 and 35.200.0.0/16 (public testing phase) — will confirm private CIDRs if we go peering.
- VPC peering: we want peering but need your template for our network team. Please have engineering share the peering acceptance template and the expected route table changes.
- Procurement contact: Looping Procurement (procurement@orbhealth.com) on this thread. They requested a short punchlist and the MAP doc you attached — I’ve forwarded the MAP to them.

We’d like a short presales technical runbook meeting — can Marissa or Neha run that? Availability: Mon 15 Mar anytime between 09:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks,
Claire Tan
Director of Product | OrbHealth
claire.tan@orbhealth.com

Subject: Re: POC readiness & quick-close checklist: org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the fast update. I’ve attached a short technical runbook and a network snippet that your infra team can paste into their firewall console. Highlights below:

Technical runbook (summary):
1) Org & Service account: once svc-redwood-poc@orbhealth.com is invited, request the following IAM scopes: Inference.Read, Inference.Run, Billing.View. We’ll only use Inference.Run for the POC.
2) API key: if you create a scoped key, add it to your secret manager and share access to the key vault path. If you prefer, we can accept a signed artifact (S3 pre-signed URL) for one-time ingestion.
3) IP allowlist: sample ranges in redwood-network-sample-cidrs.txt. For public testing the two CIDRs Claire listed are fine; for peering we’ll switch to private CIDR routes.
4) VPC peering: required details — VPC ID, account/project ID, region, and the maintenance window. We’ll generate a peering request and a small change to the route table (no NAT changes required for egress).

I can run the presales session on Mon 15 Mar at 10:00 PT. I’ll send a calendar invite to the thread. Agenda (20 min):
- 5 min: goals & acceptance criteria for the POC
- 10 min: walk the runbook (keys, allowlist, peering steps)
- 5 min: confirm timeline + procurement handoff

Attachments: redwood-network-sample-cidrs.txt, POC-runbook-short.pdf

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
